## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets—often via reciprocal rank fusion—to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on queries mixing rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) with natural language intent. It has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.

### Reciprocal Rank Fusion

Reciprocal rank fusion is the standard technique for merging results from multiple ranked retrieval methods, combining their rankings into a single coherent set.
